venue.name: Discover the Past Walking Tours
venue.description: Discover the Past Walking Tours is a family-run company founded by local historian John Adams that runs guided walking tours of downtown Victoria. Its regular tours are Ghostly Walks, daytime history walks, Chinatown walks and French-language tours; most Ghostly Walks and History Walks begin outside the Visitor Information Centre at 812 Wharf Street. Walks last 60 to 90 minutes and cover between roughly 1.5 and 3 kilometres of walking downtown. The company also tailors student tours for groups from preschool to post-grad at a discounted rate, requested through a form on its site.
restrictions: please be aware that some of the content on our Ghostly Walks tours might not be suitable for young children
Unfortunately, our Chinatown Walks tours are not suitable for four-legged friends as we go into a venue that does not allow dogs.
All bookings must be made online, in advance of the tour start time.
venue.hours_notes: Public tour prices are Adults (18+) $24, Seniors (65+) $19, Students (12-17 or with a valid student card) $19, Children (6-11) $14, and kids 5 and under free. Chinatown Walks take place year-round on Saturdays at 10:30 am (except Christmas and New Year's Day). Student tours can be scheduled at any time of the day or night.
venue.seasonal_notes: Ghostly Walks run year-round. From the beginning of June until Labour Day the historical walking tours run every day; during the rest of the year they run at weekends only unless by special arrangement. During December the company walks its Christmas in Old Victoria route.

programs.name: Student and school group tour
programs.description: Tailored tours for school and student groups, chosen from Ghostly Walk, History Walk, Chinatown Walk, White Jade Tiger, Visite en francais or a custom program. Tours can be scheduled at any time of day or night, and with enough notice several classes can be accommodated at the same time. School groups get a special rate that is a saving on the normal per-person fees, but that rate is not published. Requested through the form on the student tours page.
programs.what_children_do: Walk a route through downtown Victoria with a storyteller guide for the length of the tour chosen, stopping at the buildings and street corners where the stories happened.
programs.our_note: Everything about this one is arranged by email or form, including the price, so send the age of the group and the number of students and ask for a written quote. If you are booking for under-sixes, say so - the Ghostly Walks content is flagged as possibly unsuitable for young children.
programs.practical_summary: Tours are entirely outdoors on city streets with 1.5 to 3 kilometres of walking and no published wet-weather alternative. Price, group size limits, notice period, washrooms and lunch space are all unstated.
programs.extra_fees_note: A special school rate is offered but the amount is not published.
programs.evidence: We offfer school groups a special rate that represents a significant savings over our normal per person fees.

programs.name: Chinatown tour for K through Grade 3
programs.description: A Chinatown walking tour for the youngest students, focused on visual symbols: the murals depicting a Chinese family, Chinese students and a Chinatown street scene, the Gate of Harmonious Interest as a way to explain feng shui, red lanterns, the upturned eaves on the Chinese Public School roof, and dragons. Includes stories well known to Chinese children that explain what is going on in Chinatown today. Cost $150 for the group.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through Chinatown looking at murals, the Gate of Harmonious Interest, lanterns, rooflines and dragons, take part in a lion dance, play a Chinese game and learn to count to four in Cantonese.
programs.our_note: This is the only offering written for children under about eight, and the $150 is for the group rather than per child, so a full class costs the same as a half one. It is all on foot outdoors on public sidewalks, so plan a washroom stop before you start.
programs.practical_summary: A group-priced outdoor walking tour in Chinatown with hands-on moments built in. Duration, group size, notice period, washrooms and any wet-weather plan are not published.
programs.evidence: Our tours for K through Grade 3 focus on visual symbols: the colourful murals that depict a Chinese family

programs.name: Chinatown tour for Grade 4 through 12
programs.description: A Chinatown tour built after consultation with the teacher about specific needs and learning outcomes. Popular topics include general Chinatown history, reasons for coming to Canada, immigration stories and hardships, becoming Canadian, Chinese customs, Chinese New Year, and ancient Chinese culture and symbols. Tours include storytelling, hands-on activities and demonstrations. Cost $150 for the group. The company can also help arrange lunch in one of Chinatown's restaurants afterwards.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the streets and alleys of Chinatown with a guide, hearing immigration and settlement stories on the spot and taking part in hands-on activities and demonstrations along the way.
programs.our_note: The topics are set with you beforehand, so come to the request form with your unit already in mind. Adding the Tam Kung Temple visit costs an extra $1 per student paid to the temple, which is easy to forget in a budget.
programs.practical_summary: Group-priced outdoor walking tour with an optional temple stop for $1 per student. Duration, group size, notice period and facilities along the route are not published.
programs.extra_fees_note: To enhance your tour of Chinatown, we can take you to the Tam Kung Temple (the oldest Chinese temple in Canada). A donation of $1/student to the temple is required.
programs.evidence: Our tours include storytelling, hands-on activities and demonstrations. Cost $150.

programs.name: White Jade Tiger Chinatown tour
programs.description: A Chinatown tour for Grade 5 and Grade 6 built around the characters, places and themes of Julie Lawson's novel White Jade Tiger, offered under agreement with the author. Cost $160 for the group.
programs.what_children_do: Visit the "Never Ending Store", play fan tan in Fan Tan Alley, find an 1881 quarter in a lai see envelope, see where Dragon Maker may have lived, and try on the clothing Jasmine wore when she was transported back in time.
programs.our_note: This only works if the class has read the book - it is built on the novel rather than on Chinatown generally. It is $10 more than the standard Chinatown tour because of the author agreement.
programs.practical_summary: Group-priced outdoor walking tour in Chinatown with props and hands-on stops. Duration, group size, notice period and washroom access are not published.
programs.evidence: This tour is offered under agreement with Julie Lawson. Cost $160.

capacity - no maximum or minimum group size published; the site only says several classes can be accommodated at the same time with enough notice
lead time - 'enough notice' is the only guidance; no minimum notice in days is published
duration of the school tours - not published; the published 60 and 90 minute figures are for the public tours
chaperone ratio and whether accompanying adults are charged - not published

washrooms along the tour routes - not published

deposit, payment timing and cancellation terms - not published
